messages:
elaine: Proposing a 'variance allowance' for reserved pools — small flexible buffer customers can dip into during short bursts without falling back to open pool. Need to decide sizing, billing signal, and SLA semantics.

mike: +1. Important to define autoscale interaction. If buffer is consumed for >10m should it count against committed units or trigger preemptive reclaim?

raj: Can we leverage predictive autoscale signals instead of a purely reactive buffer? If we prewarm cheaper spot-backed nodes ahead of predicted spikes we might avoid drawing the allowance.

olga: Sales keeps hearing customers ask for "grace headroom". They want predictable billing: a clear rule for when allowance is free vs billed.

carlos: Proposal: two-tier allowance. Soft tier = free, very short window (e.g., 10-30m / small percent of daily commit). Hard tier = billable overflow at a premium. Soft tier protects SLA; hard tier is explicit fallback.

elaine: Draft SLA change idea: soft allowance = 5% of daily committed RU (resv units) or 30min of GPU time, whichever smaller, resets midnight UTC. Hard allowance billed at 1.2x unit rate. Also define a usage window threshold (10m) after which we flip from soft->hard. Feedback?

mike: Implementation note: autoscaler currently treats reservation as fixed target. We'll add config fields on pool: buffer_size (GPU-minutes / RU), buffer_ttl (seconds) and buffer_mode (soft|hard). Example config snippet:
```yaml
pool: customer-A-reserved
capacity: 64gpus
buffer:
  buffer_size: 1800 # seconds of prewarmable headroom
  buffer_mode: soft
  buffer_ttl: 600 # seconds before counting against commit
```
This lets scheduler decide to prewarm or consume buffer.

raj: Operational concerns: how do we surface this to oncall? Need alert when buffer >50% consumed for 10m and customer usage would breach their SLA if allowance spent. Also need a dashboard card per-customer: buffer_used, buffer_ttl_remaining, predicted_breach_prob.

olga: For contracting, sales needs a template clause: define soft allowance amount, billing multiplier for hard allowance, and an opt-out. Also migration path for existing customers — will old committed accounts keep current behavior unless they opt into allowance?

elaine: Action items: 1) Mike to prototype pool buffer params and a basic scheduler heuristic; 2) Raj to spec alerts and dashboard UX; 3) Carlos/Olga to draft billing language + migration comms. Target: run a small experiment with 3 pilot customers next sprint. :rocket:

mike: sgtm, I'll PR a prototype branch and attach a quick sim for common burst patterns. Ping me for test tenants.
